fair_value.method: Blend of a pro-forma (post-ASM, post-VAC, ~331M shares) sum-of-the-parts at ~$8.2/share, a discounted 2028 EV/EBITDA at ~$8.4/share, and a 50% haircut to the ~$24 sell-side consensus target ($12). I weighted them 0.5/0.3/0.2, which gives ~$9.0, then rounded up to $9.5 for the scarcity premium on US critical minerals.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Pro forma after VAC closes, 331M basic shares (65.853M VAC shares = 19.9%). Segment EVs: uranium $1.2B (~2M lb/yr, ~$23/lb cost vs ~$85 realized, ~$120M EBITDA x 10x); REE $1.1B (Vara Mada $1.8B NPV risked 25% = $0.45B; Donald 49% of A$759M pre-tax NPV8 risked 50% = ~$0.12B; White Mesa Phase 1 heavy REE $0.15B plus Phase 2 NdPr option $0.4B); VAC $1.4B (FY25 adj. EBITDA $29M, $65-75M at 2,000 tpa Sumter, ~15-18x forward, below the ~$2.04B EV paid); ASM $0.14B (roughly what was paid); corporate G&A capitalized at -$0.3B. EV ~$3.54B less pro-forma net debt/preferred ~$0.84B (~$850M YE26 liquidity - $718M VAC cash + $700M converts at $20.34 conversion + $140M VAC net debt + $135M preferred) = equity ~$2.70B / 331M.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2028E pro-forma EBITDA ~$240M (uranium $130M + VAC $120M at ~4,000 tpa + heavy REE $40M - corporate $50M) x 18x strategic-minerals multiple = $4.3B EV, discounted 1 yr at 12% = $3.85B; less ~$1.0B net debt after 2027 capex (Phase 1B/1C $78M in 2027, Donald earn-in ~A$126M) = $2.85B / ~340M shares (allowing modest further issuance).

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Sell-side consensus 12-month target ~$24.15 (8 analysts; Cantor $29.25), haircut 50%. These targets have repeatedly assumed full REE execution, and Zacks consensus has 2027 EPS at only $0.03 on $225M revenue.

bear.story: Rare earth scarcity premium keeps fading as US-China relations thaw after the Xi visit. VAC closes with a full $135M preferred make-whole and heavy cash use, which leaves net debt, and the company raises equity at depressed prices to fund Phase 2 / Donald / Vara Mada. The Vara Mada fiscal terms stall, uranium drifts to the low $70s, and losses persist through 2027.

base.story: Uranium stays around $85-95/lb with ~2M lb/yr at ~$23/lb costs. VAC closes in early 2027 and integration is noisy, the heavy REE circuits come online on schedule at end-2027, Donald reaches FID, and some dilution occurs. The stock trades sideways around a slight premium to fundamental value, carried by strategic optionality.

bull.story: A renewed China export squeeze or a US policy push (OSC $725M loan drawn, offtakes, price floors) re-rates Western mine-to-magnet names. VAC Sumter ramps, Tb/Dy qualification converts into contracts, Vara Mada fiscal terms are signed and reach FID, and uranium goes above $100. The stock heads back toward the ~$20-24 consensus.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$6.50 the pro-forma equity (~$2.1B post-VAC) would sit well below even a risk-weighted SOTP. That would most likely mean something fundamental broke rather than ordinary volatility: a distressed or highly dilutive financing (the VAC $718M cash leg plus $700M converts leave little cushion), a failed or renegotiated VAC close, Madagascar walking back Vara Mada terms, or a uranium price collapse.

catalysts.event: Donald Project FID (Astron JV; EF earn-in ~A$126M at construction start)

US-China trade negotiations after Xi's Sept 24 Washington visit; any easing of rare earth export controls

VAC acquisition close (regulatory approvals; preferred issuance if price < $20.93; Goldman $250M term loan)
Possible equity raise / OSC loan finalization to fund Phase 2 and project pipeline
Q1-2027 results, first quarter with VAC consolidated
Q2-2027 results; progress on Tb/Dy circuits targeted end-2027

key_uncertainties: Financing path for the VAC cash leg ($718M) plus Phase 2/Donald/Vara Mada capex, and the resulting dilution
Whether the geopolitical rare earth scarcity premium survives a US-China thaw
VAC earnings ramp (FY25 adj. EBITDA only $29M vs $1.9B equity paid)
Uranium price path (spot ~$90, term ~$96.5) and 2027 production guidance, which has not been given
Madagascar political/fiscal risk after the October 2025 coup
Very high realized volatility (89%) in a retail- and theme-driven stock
reasoning: Energy Fuels (UUUU) is the largest US uranium producer (1.7M lb in H1-26 at ~$23/lb, spot ~$90) and is turning itself into a 'mine-to-magnet' rare earth platform: ASM closed Aug 28, 2026; VAC ($1.9B: $718M cash + 65.85M shares + assumed $140M debt + up to $135M preferred) is due to close in early 2027; heavy REE circuits at White Mesa are under construction; and Donald and Vara Mada are pending. The stock fell from $27.90 to $11.35. Drivers: an expensive VAC deal (~65x FY25 EBITDA) that implies meaningful dilution, a Q2 EPS miss (-$0.13 vs -$0.03), downward estimate revisions (Zacks Rank 5), the rare earth sector derating on US-China thaw hopes, and Madagascar delays. Liquidity is large today (~$936M cash + securities) but largely offset by the $700M converts, and the VAC cash leg turns it into net debt. My SOTP and discounted-EBITDA methods both land at ~$8-8.5/share on a pro-forma 331M+ share base. Blended with a haircut to the bullish sell-side ($24 average target), that gives fair value ~$9.5, modestly below the current price: the market is already paying for some optionality. For the distribution I used a lognormal centered slightly below spot (median ~$10.8, reflecting fair value below price and negative estimate momentum, partly offset by thematic squeeze potential) with σ≈0.75. That is a bit under the 89% trailing vol, because the stock sits near its 52-week low after a bubble-and-unwind and has a large liquid-asset floor. I thinned the far-left tail (P≥$4.54 ≈ 0.90) for the cash/uranium floor and kept a fat right tail (P≥$23 ≈ 0.15), because rare earth policy shocks have repeatedly doubled these names. Scenario expected value ≈ $12.2 against a median ≈ $10.8, which is consistent with right skew. Research relied on ~12 web searches/fetches. I did not use option data.
